acceptanceCriteria: A lane on a host whose Homebrew Go moved past the pinned patch can still run make go-version-gated targets (windows-vet, gate steps) against the pinned go1.27.2 without manual toolchain work, or gets one refusal naming the exact install command
The documented recovery is verified on this host
body: On 2026-10-20 at 21:12Z Homebrew upgraded /opt/homebrew/Cellar/go to 1.27.3 and removed 1.27.2. Makefile go-version requires GOTOOLCHAIN=local go env GOVERSION = go1.27.2, so every local target that depends on it (make windows-vet, build, gate steps) now fails on this host. Observed by the V1-2111 lane: make windows-vet stopped at go-version; the lane ran the two Windows vet commands directly with go1.27.3 instead, which is weaker evidence than the pinned toolchain. Expected: lanes keep a pinned toolchain that a package-manager upgrade cannot remove (for example golang.org/dl/go1.27.2 under ~/sdk with GOROOT selection in the Makefile), or a clear one-step recovery. Actual: an unattended brew upgrade silently breaks every local pinned check. Related: V1-0429 (darwin tests pinned to the Homebrew Go).
